title: Capitalise Each Word
description: Read a single line of text and print it with the first letter of every word in uppercase and the rest in lowercase. Words are separated by single spaces.
hint: Split on spaces, capitalise each word, then join them back together with a space.

io.input: A single line of words separated by spaces.

starter_code:

# print the text with each word capitalised
solution:

words = text.split(' ')
print(' '.join(word.capitalize() for word in words))

# print True if the two are anagrams (ignore case & spaces)

title: Run-Length Encoding
description: Read a single line of text and print its run-length encoding: each run of the same character is replaced by that character followed by the run length. For example, 'aaabbc' becomes 'a3b2c1'.
hint: Walk the string, grouping consecutive equal characters, and append the character plus its count.
starter_code:
text = input()
# print the run-length encoding, e.g. aaabb -> a3b2
solution:
text = input()
result = ''
index = 0
while index < len(text):
    char = text[index]
    run = 0
    while index < len(text) and text[index] == char:
        run += 1
        index += 1
    result += char + str(run)
print(result)
description_xh: Funda umgca omnye wombhalo uze uprinte ukubhalwa kwawo: umgca ngamnye wesimboli esifanayo uthatyathelwa indawo yile nto ilandelwa ngumgca. Ngokomzekelo, i-'aaabbc' iba yi-'a3b2c1'.
hint_xh: Hamba kwistring, uqokelele oonobumba abalinganayo ngokulandelelana, uze ufake oonobumba kunye nenani labo.

title: Run-Length Decoding
description: Read a run-length encoded line such as 'a3b2c1' and print the text it stands for: every character is followed by the number of times it repeats. Counts may have more than one digit.
hint: After reading a character, keep collecting the digits that follow it until the next non-digit. char * int(digits) repeats the character that many times.
starter_code:
text = input()
# print the decoded text, e.g. a3b2 -> aaabb
solution:
text = input()
result = ''
index = 0
while index < len(text):
    char = text[index]
    index += 1
    digits = ''
    while index < len(text) and text[index].isdigit():
        digits += text[index]
        index += 1
    result += char * int(digits)
print(result)
description_xh: Funda umgca onobude obude obunjengokuthi 'a3b2c1' uze uprinte umbhalo omelayo: umlinganiswa ngamnye ulanjelwa linani lamaxesha aphindaphindwayo.
hint_xh: Emva kokufunda umlinganiswa, qhubeka uqoqa amanani alandelayo de kube ngumlinganiswa ongekho kwinani elilandelayo. char * int(digits) iphinda umlinganiswa lowo izihlandlo ezininzi.

title: First Unique Character
description: Read a single line of text and print the first character that appears exactly once. If every character is repeated, print None.
hint: text.count(char) tells you how often a character appears in the whole line. Walk the text in order and stop at the first character whose count is 1.

io.output: The first non-repeating character, or None.

starter_code:
text = input()
# print the first character that appears only once, or None
solution:
text = input()
answer = None
for char in text:
    if text.count(char) == 1:
        answer = char
        break
print(answer)
description_xh: Funda umgca omnye wesicatshulwa uze uprinte umlinganiswa wokuqala ovela kanye kuphela. Ukuba wonke umlinganiswa uyaphindaphindwa, printa None.
hint_xh: text.count(char) ikuxelela ukuba umlinganiswa uvela kaninzi kangakanani kumgca wonke. Hamba umbhalo ngokulandelana uze ume kumlinganiswa wokuqala onokubala kwakhe ngu-1.

io_xh.output: Umlinganiswa wokuqala ongenzi nto, okanye uNone.

title: Most Common Word
description: Read a single line of words and print the word that appears most often. If two words appear the same number of times, print the one that comes first in the line.
hint: Split the line into a list of words, then use words.count(word) on each one. Only replace your best answer when you find a strictly larger count, so earlier words win ties.

io.input: A single line of words separated by spaces.

starter_code:
text = input()
# print the word that appears most often
solution:
words = input().split()
best = ''
best_count = 0
for word in words:
    count = words.count(word)
    if count > best_count:
        best = word
        best_count = count
print(best)

tests.input: the cat the dog the bird

description_xh: Funda umgca nje omnye wamagama uze uprinte igama elivela rhoqo. Ukuba amagama amabini avela kaninzi, printa elivela kuqala.
hint_xh: Yahlula umgca ube yi-list yamagama, uze usebenzise i-words.count(word) kumagama ngalinye. Yenza kuphela impendulo yakho efanelekileyo xa ufumana inani elikhulu, ukuze amagama angaphambi kwexesha aphumelele.
